history.dynasty: Portuguese colonial period (relocated 1567); present structure 18th century
history.summary: CSV town is WRONG: this temple is at Veling (Mardol), Ponda taluka, North Goa - not Vasco da Gama. Dedicated to Narasimha, the fourth (man-lion) avatar of Vishnu, with his consort Lakshmi. The temple was moved from Sancoale (Sankhavali) in Salcete to Ponda in 1567 to save the deities from destruction during the Portuguese temple destructions; the current structure dates to the 18th century. It is known for intricate carvings depicting tales from the Narasimha Purana, a hall showcasing the various avatars of Vishnu, and a stepped laterite pushkar (water tank) shaded by coconut palms in front of the temple. Consulted sources do not publish fixed daily opening hours or a full festival calendar beyond Narasimha Jayanti.

name: Shree Lakshmi Narasimha Temple
town_description: Veling is a small village in Ponda taluka, North Goa, near Mardol. It sits in the temple-dense Ponda region and is known chiefly for its ancient Narasimha shrine set among coconut palms.

travel.airport: Goa International Airport, Dabolim (~25-30 km) or Manohar International Airport, Mopa
travel.railway: Karmali or Thivim (~20-25 km); Madgaon Junction (~25 km)
travel.road: Accessible by road via Ponda town (~5 km) on the Panaji-Ponda route.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Narasimha Jayanti draws the largest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published in consulted sources; visitors report early-morning and late-afternoon visits as best. Photography inside the temple is discouraged.
